title: Permits that need another permit first
question: Which permits only exist because of, or on top of, another permit?
finding: The records show 77,490 instances since 2015 of a permit that points back at, or waits on, another permit or approval (one permit can appear in more than one row): 12,686 Public Works street permits quote a building permit application, 3,855 building projects were approved as a site permit followed by 7,403 separate sets of construction drawings, each routed for approval again, 8,636 building permits carry a reviewer's note that Public Works must sign off or issue its own permit before the job can be closed, and 8,860 building permits exist only to finish or renew an earlier one.
how: Counted from the records themselves: street-use permits whose record carries a building permit application number; building permits whose stated purpose quotes an earlier permit or a violation notice; site permits with later addenda in the routing table; full-review building permits listed on a Planning project record; and the notes City reviewers wrote on the routing record.
limits: Pointing at an earlier permit is not proof the earlier one was legally required first; a clerk may enter the number for cross-reference. Some dependence is sensible: nobody should dig up a sidewalk for a building that is not approved. The data shows the dependence exists and how common it is. It does not show a true catch-22 (two permits that each require the other first); proving one needs the written rules for each permit, which are being collected.

rows.kind: Full-review building permit or new building
Building permit filed to answer a violation notice or complaint
rows.needs: The notice or complaint it answers

rows.kind: Building permit approved with a reviewer's note tying it to Public Works (sign-off on the job card before the final inspection, a street improvement, sidewalk, encroachment or tree permit)
rows.needs: A Public Works permit or sign-off

rows.kind: Building permit taken out only to finish, renew or reinstate an earlier building permit
Construction addenda: separate sets of drawings approved one by one after the site permit
Building permit that says part of the same job is under a separate permit (most often sprinklers, fire alarm, mechanical, electrical or plumbing)
rows.needs: Another building permit for the rest of the job

rows.kind: Building permit held or noted for a water and sewer capacity charge
rows.needs: Payment of the Public Utilities Commission charge

rows.kind: Public Works permits in the new 2026 system (all kinds)
Building permit noted for the soil-contamination (Maher) rules
